author: T.R. Pomeroy
title: Andvari’s Ring: When Treasure Becomes Obsession
summary: What does a cursed ring ask of us? A short reflection on wanting, keeping, and the fear of losing.
context: This is the author’s personal reading of Andvari’s curse, not a claim about every Norse person’s beliefs. In chapter 14 of Völsunga saga, Andvari curses the stolen ring and gold; Fafnir kills his father, takes the hoard and becomes a dragon. The modern parallels in this excerpt belong to the author’s reflection.
editorial_note: Selected reflection passages from the episode manuscript, with spoken line breaks joined for reading. The author’s wording is preserved; the context distinguishes literary interpretation from historical evidence.

paragraphs: So what is the lesson of the cursed ring? Is it simply: “Don’t be greedy”? Or does the curse run deeper—into the marrow of power, the nature of fate, the soul of ambition? Because this ring—didn’t just end lives. It corrupted love. It turned fathers against sons, brothers into monsters, heroes into betrayers. The Norse myths don’t warn us that gold will kill us. They whisper that the love of it might.
Let’s turn the mirror for a moment. Imagine a gift. A ring. You’re told it can bring you abundance. Power. Security. You tell yourself you’ll use it for good.
But as the gold gathers, so does fear. What if someone takes it? What if you lose it? What if… it’s never enough? And suddenly, the thing that freed you… enslaves you.
This is the deepest truth of the cursed ring. Not that it kills. But that it binds. Not in chains. In obsession.

The saga of Andvari’s ring teaches us that the curse is never just in the gold. It’s in the way it changes you. Because sometimes, the greatest evil isn’t a dragon. It’s the man who forgets who he used to be.

In Norse myth, the ring is a curse because it amplifies desire. It takes what you want—and turns it into what you cannot live without. That’s why it’s still relevant. Because we live in a world obsessed with more. More wealth. More power. More reach. More success. And sometimes, in chasing more… we lose our way.

The ring is ancient. But its curse? It’s still active. We may not find it in treasure chests or blacksmiths’ forges. But we find it in promotions. In platforms. In bank accounts. The question is never “Do I want it?” The question is: “What will I become if I get it?”
